message.content:
Review target: `2752`

That target is GitHub pull request 2752, and its own diff is this review's scope. Get the diff with this command, run alone, with nothing chained, piped or redirected:

```
gh pr diff 2752
```

It replaces every `git diff` command that the instructions below give for gathering the diff. This checkout may be on another branch, and must stay as it is: before you lean on a file here for context, check that it already has the diff's added lines, and where it does not, judge from the diff alone and report nothing from that file. If you start subagents, give each one the diff itself and this warning: they see none of this.

Some sessions have a gh with no `pr diff` command. Only if gh itself says so, run this in its place, alone too:

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/2752 -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.diff'
```

If that leaves you without the diff, because a command was refused or failed, go on as if this section were not here: follow the instructions below, and post the findings as they say. Then open your final reply with this sentence, word for word: "Could not read GitHub pull request 2752: `gh pr diff 2752` was refused or failed, so this review and its comments are of the checked-out code."

Use the quoted words only where you could not read the diff. Where you did read it, leave them out altogether.

`low effort → 1 diff pass (bugs) → no verify → ≤4 findings`

## Turn 1 — read

One tool call: read the unified diff (`git diff origin/HEAD...HEAD; git diff HEAD`
to cover both committed and uncommitted changes, or `git diff main...HEAD` /
the target passed as an argument). Skip test/fixture
hunks (`test/`, `spec/`, `__tests__/`, `*_test.*`, `*.test.*`,
`fixtures/`, `testdata/`) — test-file changes are not reviewed at this level.
No subagents, no full-file reads.

## Turn 2 — findings

Flag runtime-correctness bugs visible from the hunk alone: inverted/wrong
condition, off-by-one, null/undefined deref where adjacent lines show the value
can be absent, removed guard, falsy-zero check, missing `await`,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in a catch that should propagate.

Do **not** flag style, naming, perf, missing tests, or anything outside the
hunk.

Output at most **4 findings**, most-severe first, one line each:
`path/to/file.ext:123 — important|pre_existing|nit — what's wrong and the concrete failure. Fix: the change to make, or what to check if you are not sure`. Every line carries one of those three words: `important` (a bug that this change adds or makes worse, even if the trigger is rare), `pre_existing` (a bug that was there before this change) or `nit` (a bug that harms nobody). That is also the order, most severe first. Report a mistake repeated in several places once, and name the other places. If nothing
qualifies, output exactly `(none)`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available.


## Posting to GitHub (--comment)

The `--comment` flag was passed. After producing the findings list, if the
review target is a GitHub PR, post each finding as an inline PR comment via
`mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment` (one call per finding;
include a suggestion block only when it fully fixes the issue). Open each finding's text with its severity in words, never with an emoji:
"Important:", "Pre-existing (not from this change, not blocking):" or "Nit (optional):". If that tool
is not available in this session, fall back to `gh api` (repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments)
or print the findings instead. If the target is not a PR, print the findings
to the terminal and note that `--comment` was ignored.

diff --git a/backend/tests/db/test_retention_sweep_indexes.py b/backend/tests/db/test_retention_sweep_indexes.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..133b5ceb3
--- /dev/null
+++ b/backend/tests/db/test_retention_sweep_indexes.py
@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
+"""Each retention sweep, as the code builds it, reaches the partial index written for it (#2751).
+
+The statement is compiled by the session's own dialect and sent through the driver, so the
+planner sees the text the app sends. A hand-written copy of the query would prove only that the
+copy matches the index.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+from sqlalchemy import null, text
+
+from backend.app.services import run_service
+from backend.tests.support.driver_guard import assert_client_side_binding
+from backend.tests.support.index_plans import drop_rival_indexes
+
+_CUTOFF = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
+
+_SWEEPS: list[tuple[str, Callable[[], list[Any]], dict[str, Any]]] = [
+    (
+        "ix_results_unpurged_created",
+        run_service.sample_failures_guard,
+        {"sample_failures": null(), "sample_failures_purged_at": _CUTOFF},
+    ),
+    ("ix_results_unpurged_observed", run_service.observed_list_guard, {"observed_value": null()}),
+    (
+        "ix_results_unpurged_unparsed",
+        run_service.observed_unparsed_guard,
+        {"observed_value": null()},
+    ),
+]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("index", "guard", "values"), _SWEEPS, ids=[s[0] for s in _SWEEPS])
+def test_the_sweep_the_code_builds_reaches_its_index(
+    db_session: Any, index: str, guard: Callable[[], list[Any]], values: dict[str, Any]
+) -> None:
+    connection = db_session.connection()
+    assert_client_side_binding(connection)
+    drop_rival_indexes(connection, index)
+    connection.execute(text("SET LOCAL enable_seqscan = off"))
+    statement = run_service.purge_statement(
+        cutoff=_CUTOFF, extra_where=guard(), values=values, chunk_size=500
+    )
+    compiled = statement.compile(dialect=connection.dialect)
+    plan = "\n".join(
+        row[0] for row in connection.exec_driver_sql(f"EXPLAIN {compiled}", compiled.params)
+    )
+    assert index in plan, f"the sweep misses {index}:\n{plan}"

+++ b/changelog.d/2751.fixed.md
@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+**The retention sweep of list-shaped observed values uses its index.** The daily sweep that
+scrubs old list-shaped `observed_value`s was compiled in a form PostgreSQL could not match to the
+index built for it, so every chunk scanned the whole `results` table. It now reads only the
+expired rows.
